# macOS paired harness transaction

The `harness-transaction` job in `.github/workflows/darwin-hq-install.yml` runs on a disposable GitHub-hosted Apple Silicon macOS 27 runner. It builds ordinary Machine and a separate Go test overlay. The latter recognizes one reproducible ACP fixture at one fixed pathname and digest, with empty arguments and two fixed adapter/account mappings. The workflow keeps both binaries on the runner.

The normal first-HQ and dedicated pairing flows use the test-overlay Machine daemon from the outset and pin a disposable software owner. The existing paired account fixture uses the ordinary, unmodified Machine CLI to plan and apply the two account and broker-directory changes, with the paired test daemon checking the owner approval. It checks the account identities, private groups and homes, endpoint ownership and modes, one-use receipt, and a repeat plan with zero changes. Those reviewed endpoints are retained for the launch test.

The paired test daemon stays running throughout, so its own launcher digest matches the launch plan. After account provisioning, the test-overlay CLI builds the launch plan and executes the fixture-only mapping. Packaged HQ exports and returns each Machine-signed launch challenge. Identity's typed Swift parser checks the full canonical install or retirement plan before the fixture signs its distinct transcript. For installation, ordinary Machine must first decline the unqualified adapter without spending its approval. The overlay then applies the same plan. Each operation is applied twice and the test checks the original positive receipt stays byte-identical.

A controller running as dedicated HQ invokes the installed sudo rule, launcher and sandbox. For each new OS account it checks the kernel UID/GID on both sockets, verifies the member hello and broker HMAC, and waits for the ACP response and supervisor closure record. Before check-in, the fixture adapter must receive sandbox permission errors for reachable direct IPv4 and IPv6 listeners and a reachable sibling socket in its assigned account's endpoint directory. The member and broker listeners are local test peers. The test checks the sudo rule, launcher, profile and policy are gone after retirement and both accounts retain their original homes. GitHub discards these fixture accounts and their data with the runner.

Production vendor-adapter qualification, physical owner presence, and the complete packaged HQ/Souls runtime and production broker remain independent gates. This job does not select a protected profile.
